'''Santa Monica''' was a pre-War city in [[Los Angeles]] County, [[California]] which appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Before the Great War, Santa Monica was a famous tourist destination mostly for the [[Santa Monica Pier]], which is largely still standing by [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. It was also the home to [[Vault 33]], which was constructed just south of the Santa Monica Pier in a bunker-like building along the coast.

==Appearances==
Santa Monica appears in the ''[[Fallout (TV series)|Fallout]]'' television series, although the area corresponding to it is visible on the [[Fallout map|first ''Fallout'' game's world map]] as well.

==Behind the scenes==
The Santa Monica Pier was filmed at [[wikipedia:Elizabeth Bay|Elizabeth Bay, Namibia]], a ghost town and former diamond mine. Visual effects were used to add the pier's Ferris wheel and roller coaster, as well as the Malibu Mountains in the background, but everything else in the shots was practical.<ref>[https://archive.ph/A5p5K Los Angeles Times: "In ‘Fallout,’ a destroyed L.A. comes to life, with some help from ... Namibia?"]</ref>

This '''Starlight Drive-in Theatre''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Background==
This small drive-in theater, operated by [[Starlight Theaters]], was located somewhere on the outskirts of [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]]. By the time of the [[Great War]], the theater was offering a double feature showing of ''[[A Man and His Dog|A Man and His Dog 3]]'' at 6:30 PM and another film involving Dracula later in the night.<ref>[[:File:FOTV S2E1 Starlight Drive-in Theatre.png|Theater marquee]]</ref>

The theater was also used as the site of [[Vault 24]], the entrance of which was hidden behind the movie screen.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Innovator]]===
[[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] and [[the Ghoul]] come across the theater during their journey to [[New Vegas]], following in the tracks of [[Hank MacLean]]. While the Ghoul is initially drawn to the theater marquee, as it listed one of his old movies (''A Man and His Dog 3''), Lucy's attention is immediately caught by the open door of Vault 24 behind the tattered movie screen. They soon enter the Vault to follow Hank, who did the same thing.

==Appearances==
The Starlight Drive-in Theatre appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

'''Santa Monica Pier''' was a pre-War attraction in [[Los Angeles|Los Angeles County]], [[California]] which appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Located in [[Santa Monica]], California, Santa Monica Pier was a popular tourist attraction which included a small amusement park (with a Ferris wheel and roller coasters), concession stands, and areas for viewing the [[Pacific Ocean]]. The entrance to [[Vault 33]] was built just slightly further inland from the pier.

As of 2296, much of the pier up to its Ferris wheel is still standing, but the sections further past have collapsed into the ocean. Save for some scattered buildings and the now-exposed entrance of Vault 33, most of the surrounding area has been desertified, with little remaining of the urban ruins of Santa Monica proper.

==Appearances==
The Santa Monica Pier appears {{in|FOTV}}, in the episode "[[The End (episode)|The End]]" and its end credits. It also appears in a pre-War flashback in the episode "[[The Innovator]]." The corresponding area is also visible on the [[Fallout map|first ''Fallout'' game's world map]].

==Behind the scenes==
The Santa Monica Pier was filmed at [[wikipedia:Elizabeth Bay|Elizabeth Bay, Namibia]], a ghost town and former diamond mine. Visual effects were used to add the pier's Ferris wheel and roller coaster, as well as the Malibu Mountains in the background, but everything else in the shots was practical.<ref>[https://archive.ph/A5p5K Los Angeles Times: "In ‘Fallout,’ a destroyed L.A. comes to life, with some help from ... Namibia?"]</ref>

'''Affordable Al's Discount Hospital''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
A private pre-War hospital, the six-storey Affordable Al's was advertised as offering advantageous prices, including "revolutionary treatments" for the [[New Plague]] at low rates, [[lobotomy|lobotomies]] at half price, and comprehensive weight loss programs (on top of other hospital services, such as emergency rooms and surgery). After the [[Great War]], the hospital was abandoned, with many patients left to die on the gurneys with no assistance.<ref name="fotv202">{{FOTV|2|2}}</ref>

Scavenged and damaged by centuries of neglect and the elements, it eventually became a nest for a swarm of [[Radscorpion (TV series)|radscorpions]].<ref name="fotv202"/>

==In the TV series==
===[[The Golden Rule]]===
[[Lucy MacCready|Lucy]] and [[The Ghoul]], on their way to [[Las Vegas]], investigate the hospital when they hear a [[Wounded woman|woman]] scream for help. Despite the Ghoul's insistence, she enters the hospital, with the Ghoul reluctantly following along with [[CX404]]. Exploring the derelict, skeleton-strewn building they locate the woman and a [[wounded man]] in the basement kitchen. While Lucy tends to the woman, the Ghoul kills the man after recognizing them both as respectively a [[Legion]] slave and a legionary. The commotion attracts the attention of the radscorpions, leading to a fight in which both the woman and the Ghoul are struck and poisoned by the giant radscorpion. Lucy decides to treat the woman with her only stimpak, leaving the Ghoul to slowly regenerate under CX404's watch.<ref name="fotv202"/>

===[[The Profligate]]===
Inside the ruins of the hospital, [[the Ghoul]] has managed to crawl into a pool venue, still suffering the effects of the [[Radscorpion (TV series)|radscorpion]] sting that incapacitated him. With [[CX404|Dogmeat]] beside him for company, he takes out a [[skinning knife]] and extracts the stinger tip that was left inside his thigh from the creature's attack.

==Appearances==
Affordable Al's Discount Hospital appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Golden Rule]]."

The '''headquarters of the United Nations''' is a mentioned-only location {{In|FO3}} and {{In|FOTV|noin}}.

==Background==
{{Main|United Nations}}
In May [[Timeline (2050-2099)#2052|2052]], as Earth's fossil fuel supplies began to dry up and nations began to [[Resource Wars|wage war with each other]] over the few resources that remained, the United Nations began to collapse under intense international squabbling, with many heated debates breaking out within their headquarters in [[New York City]].<ref group="Non-game">[[Fallout Bible 0#Timeline repair: Second strike|''Fallout Bible 0'']]: ''"2052 May-July: The United Nations, already suffering, begins to collapse. In a series of heated debates, many nations withdrew from the organization as the UN tried to keep the peace. At the end of July, the United Nations is disbanded."''</ref>

On July 26, 2052, at the height of global tensions over resource availability, the organization was formally disbanded. The sitting UN President at the time, [[Sakugama Okiri]], lamented the failure of global relations at a press conference held later in the building. The ambassadors of the few nations that remained in the headquarters were forced to vacate by the end of the week as a bidding war broke out over the building itself. As reported in the [[Washington, D.C.|D.C.]]-based ''[[Capital Post (company)|Capital Post]]'' newspaper, the toy company [[Bumbalo's]], in particular, hoped to turn the prime real estate into their new [[East Coast]] superstore.<ref>[[Capitol Post terminal entries#United Nations Disbanded.21|Capitol Post terminal entries; Capital Post Top Stories -- July 27, 2052, United Nations Disbanded!]]</ref>

Although the eventual buyer is unknown, training guides produced by the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] included a cartoon depiction of the UN building being overtaken with Vault-Tec logos. It remains unclear if this is a reflection of reality or merely a hyperbolic appropriation of the UN's imagery.<ref>"[[Step on the Gas!]]"</ref>

==Appearances==
The headquarters of the United Nations is mentioned only in ''Fallout 3''. A cartoon depiction appears in the ''[[Vault Seller's Survival Guide]]'' episode "[[Step on the Gas!]]"

'''Westside Medical Clinic''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in [[Los Angeles]] {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
The medical clinic was built in the [[Hollywood]] district of [[Los Angeles]], [[State#California|California]], situated along a section of the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].

By the 23rd century, the desert sands and rolling winds of the [[wasteland]] have resulted in the interior being half-buried but still accessible.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Ghouls]]===
During the trek from [[Hollywood Boulevard]] to a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] near [[Santa Monica Boulevard]], [[the Ghoul]] and [[Lucy MacLean]] pass near the Westside Medical Clinic and overhear someone shouting inside. Lucy enters at gunpoint ahead of the Ghoul, where they discover [[Roger (TV series)|Roger]], another [[ghoul]] squatting in one of the rooms, furiously shouting his name as he is on the verge of [[Feral ghoul|going feral]].

After Roger tries to get the Ghoul to share his supply of [[inhaler vial]]s only to be told he does not have any, he resigns himself to his fate, lamenting that he had managed to persevere for decades since first showing symptoms and remarking that the Ghoul himself will likely outlast the rest of them. The Ghoul helps ease Roger by getting him to remember the taste of pre-War food like [[BlamCo Mac & Cheese]], ice cream, and apple pie. Just as Roger thinks fondly on his mother's cooking, he is executed with a headshot by the Ghoul, to Lucy's shock.

As the Ghoul loots the body of his friend for valuables and then begins harvesting his teeth and flesh for "[[ass jerky]]," he asks Lucy for her name and ponders when she reveals her last name of "MacLean." After a few retorts over the Vault dweller's insistence about her mission to rescue [[Hank MacLean|her father]], the Ghoul's last insult causes Lucy to question why he continues in such a violent lifestyle which confuses and angers the bounty hunter. He then forces Lucy to finish carving up Roger's body before they leave to continue their journey.

==Appearances==
The Westside Medical Clinic appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Ghouls]]."

==Behind the scenes==
;Trivia:
* As shown in the page image, a [[Corvega]]-brand taxi can be seen parked right outside the clinic as Lucy and the Ghoul walk by.
;Filming:
* The filming set for scenes at the Westside Medical Clinic was the ''Krankenhaus'' (hospital) of the ghost town of [[wikipedia:Kolmanskop|Kolmanskop, Namibia]]. The town was also used for several other scenes, including the [[Farmer (TV series)|farmer]]'s house during the [[The Target|second episode]].

The '''yao guai cave''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in the [[Wilds]] in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Background==
As indicated by the "Hazardous Waste" signage outside and the presence of waste barrels and old equipment within, the natural cave formation was used as a disposal site for nuclear waste before the [[Great War]].

Sometime prior to [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], a [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]] claimed the cave as its nest. It preyed on surrounding wildlife and even several wastelanders with their bones and gory remains left strewn around inside.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Target]]===
Sometime after escaping from the [[Enclave research colony]], [[Siggi Wilzig]] and his companion [[CX404]] passed through the Wilds and came to a rest outside the cave. While Wilzig had a trail ration of [[Cram]], the canine wandered into the cave where it retrieved a severed human hand to bring back to its master. Wilzig realized the danger they were in as he then heard the distant roars of the yao guai prowling nearby, forcing a quick exit.

Later on, [[Knights of San Fernando|Brotherhood]] [[Titus|Knight Titus]] and his squire [[Maximus]] arrived in the area of the Wilds close to the cave by [[Vertibird (TV series)|vertibird]], after disembarking because Titus wanted "something to shoot at." They found Wilzig's abandoned campsite and evidence of his presence. Titus points out the cave and they suspect their target was taken by whatever lives inside it. The [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T60-outfitted]] knight forces his squire to walk ahead of him as they look through the cave. However, they are unaware when the yao guai returns, leading to Titus being disarmed of his [[Heavy assault rifle (TV series)|heavy assault rifle]] when it attacks him. When Maximus fails to attack on his order, he runs in terror but is taken down by the creature and lethally mauled before the squire can kill it.

Titus demands Maximus heal him with a stimpak, but continues to verbally abuse him and threaten him for his failure, leading to Maximus condemning the knight and letting him succumb to his wounds. Maximus takes Titus' uniform and his T-60 power armor to impersonate him and leaves to complete the mission to find the artifact alone.

==Appearances==
The yao guai cave appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Behind the scenes==
Scenes taking place at the yao guai cave were filmed at the [[wikipedia:Widow Jane Mine|Widow Jane Mine]] in [[wikipedia:Rosendale, New York|Rosendale, New York]].

Sonny's Sundries.original_wikitext:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |image =Sonny's Sundries.png |image desc = |part of =[[Freeside]] |owners =[[Sonny]] {{Icon|dead}}
[[Shopkeep Simon]] (ostensibly) }} '''Sonny's Sundries''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== A general store within [[Freeside]], Sonny's Sundries sold various items including sundries, weapons, medicine, and other equipment. It was owned and operated by [[Sonny]] up until July [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], when Sonny was murdered by a thief named [[Shopkeep Simon|Simon]]. Simon subsequently took over, pretending to be the shopkeeper by putting on Sonny's clothes, which were far too small for him, and heavily inflating Sonny's prices.{{FOTV|2|6}} Sonny's remains were shoved into a garbage bin inside near the back of the store. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Wrangler]]=== Suffering from a [[Buffout addiction]], [[Lucy MacLean]] is given [[bottle cap]]s by [[the Ghoul]], who tells her to go to Sonny's Sundries to purchase [[Addictol (TV series)|Addictol]] with which to clean out her system. When she reaches the store, she sees that the price for Addictol, written on a chalkboard outside the main door, has been raised to a degree that she cannot afford. Lucy is disheartened, but sees a back door left open on the side of the shop, and decides that to deal with her present circumstances she must steal a vial of Addictol from the store. Sneaking in, she finds the medicine, takes it, and pauses to inspect and additionally take a [[Power fist (TV series)|power fist]] on display, as well as a bag to hold it. While she does so, she notices a dead and bloody body stuffed into a nearby trash can—that of Sonny, though Lucy is initially unaware of this. While distracted, Shopkeep Simon sees her and confronts her, and Lucy tries to assuage the man and come across as a regular shopper. As she does so, she notices a portrait of the store owner, the dead man in the trash can. She inquires about the dead body, which Simon unconvincingly claims was an attempted thief. Lucy questions him why the man is naked, which causes Simon to defensively claim that naked robbers aren't unusual. She questions him further about why his clothes don't fit and deduces the body in the trash can is the original shopkeeper, pulling her 10mm pistol on Simon. She tries to avoid further escalation but doesn't hesitate to shoot Simon as he immediately reaches for a weapon. Lucy inspects him, finding she had shot him dead and starts reconsidering her recent actions, taking the Addictol and power fist and leaving soon after a [[Freeside customer|customer]] arrives to find her standing over Simon's corpse. Afterwards, Lucy administers the Addictol to herself outside the store, causing her to vomit horribly. ==Appearances== Sonny's Sundries appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Wrangler]]." ==Gallery== Fallout Season 2 Amazon Freeside bg.jpg|Bottom right, seen on [[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|season 2 overview on Prime Video]] FTV_S2E5_Still_106.png|[[Lucy MacLean]] swipes a [[Power fist (TV series)|power fist]] FTV_S2E5_Still_107.png|Lucy tries to hide ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Freeside buildings]] [[ru:Всячина Сонни]]

The Ghoul's grave.original_wikitext:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |factions =[[Dom Pedro (character)|Dom Pedro's]] gang }} '''The Ghoul's grave''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== At some point, [[the Ghoul]] was captured by a powerful man known as [[Dom Pedro (character)|Dom Pedro]] and brought to his stronghold. Considering the Ghoul a personal enemy,In Scene 46 of "The End," mariachi music is heard playing in the scene depicting a guard with the attire and facial hair traditionally associated with Mexican banditos and revolutionaries. The sign at the location reads "CEMENTERIO. ENEMIGOS DE DOM PEDRO," which is Spanish for "Cemetery. Enemies of Dom Pedro." Dom Pedro had the gunslinger buried alive in a grave, sustained only by an IV drip. It's said that Dom Pedro would dig up the Ghoul annually to cut off pieces of his body before reburial.[[Slim (TV series)|Slim]]: ''"How do we know which grave?"''
[[Honcho]]: ''"Well, Slim, we look for the fresh one. Dom Pedro has our friend dug up once a year. Cuts some pieces off and puts him right back in the ground."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) ==In the TV series== ===[[The End (episode)|The End]]=== Sometime in 2296, a group of bounty hunters consisting of [[Honcho]], [[Biggie]], and [[Slim (TV series)|Slim]] snuck into Dom Pedro's fortress at night, with Biggie using his [[Junk Jet (TV series)|Junk Jet]] to take out [[Dom Pedro's guard|a guard]].{{FOTV|1|1}} Honcho then explains that they are searching for a notorious bounty hunter whom Dom Pedro has held captive for several years. They eventually come upon a small graveyard, which includes one grave with a pair of IV bags and tubes emerging from the dirt. Biggie and Slim are shocked to realize the person they are looking for is a [[ghoul]], and Honcho says that his father once worked with him.[[Slim (TV series)|Slim]]: ''"Shit. You're telling me this supreme badass we're looking for is a godforsaken mutant?"''
[[Honcho]]: ''"Have some respec'. That's your prospective coworker you's talking about and our ticket to a big payoff."''
Slim: ''"Thought you said you knew this guy."''
Honcho: ''"I said I knew of him. My pop worked with him once."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) Biggie expresses concern that he may have gone [[Feral ghoul|feral]]. Honcho brings out a [[chicken]] and explains that a feral ghoul cannot tolerate them. The hunters dig up the coffin contained in the grave and place the chicken in front of it before opening it up. From inside, the Ghoul emerges, revealed to be an aged and mutated Cooper Howard. He playfully picks up the chicken, terrifying Biggie and Slim. Honcho proposes they work together to secure a large bounty. He elaborates that [[Siggi Wilzig|the target]] has gone to seek out [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] in California, specifying that he knows the Ghoul is originally from there. The Ghoul takes offense to the mention of his past and claims that, unlike them, he pursues bounties "for the love of the game." The Ghoul proceeds to kill Slim and Biggie. He then wounds Honcho and drags him over to toss him into the coffin and let it drop back into the open grave, asserting that cowpokes like him "take it as it comes." The Ghoul spares the chicken, taking it with him as he leaves to pursue the bounty alone. ==Notes== The Ghoul's introduction of being buried alive in a grave is similar to [[Coffin Willie]], who was similarly buried alive in a grave in [[Golgotha]] near [[New Reno]] for years before being dug up by the [[Chosen One]] {{In|FO2}}. ==References== {{References}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]]

The '''BBQ Shack''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Formerly a business establishment in the pre-[[Great War|War]] era in the former city of [[Santa Monica]], [[State#California|California]], sometime after the destruction of the [[New California Republic|NCR]] capital of [[Shady Sands]] in [[Timeline#2283|2283]], [[Sorrel Booker]] formed an organization of his own out of a self-righteous mission to restore order in [[Los Angeles]], naming it [[Govermint|the Govermint]] with himself as its president and claimed the old restaurant as their headquarters. From here, they conduct their operations including sending [[Sheriff (TV series)|"sheriffs"]] to collect tribute paid to them by those they secure under their protection rackets including the organ-harvesters [[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]] out of a nearby [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] outlet.

Booker's crew also seemingly maintains a small farm close to the building, raising [[hog]]s to slaughter for meat to feed themselves as well as utilizing the animals as low-tech body disposal if the need arises.

===Wanted posters===
[[File:Govermint wanted posters.png|thumb|250px|Wanted posters]]
While the legitimacy of the Govermint's bounties is questionable, the BBQ Shack's wall features an assortment of bounty posters for valuable targets, with notable ones including [[Lee Moldaver]], at least one [[Super mutant (TV series)|super mutant]], and a couple of [[ghoul]]s by [[Timeline#2w96|2296]].
{{clear}}

==In the TV series==
===[[The Trap]]===
[[File:Sorrel Booker.png|thumb|250px|Govermint "president" [[Sorrel Booker]], current owner of the BBQ Shack]]
After being picked up by sheriffs of the Govermint at the destroyed Super Duper Mart following the deaths of their clients Huey and Squirrel [[The Ghouls|a short time prior]], [[the Ghoul]] is brought to their HQ at the BBQ Shack and re-introduced to Govermint president Sorrel Booker, who recognizes the mutant bounty hunter from a past encounter and mentions his lifelong quest for "[[Janey Howard|her]]," but is brushed off by the Ghoul who instead focuses on using a needle and thread to reattach the finger previously bitten off by [[Lucy MacLean]].<ref name="FOTV0106">Events of {{FOTV|1|6}}</ref>

As Booker begins to chastise his former associate for supposedly disrupting the Govermint's business by destroying the organ harvesting operation, the Ghoul taunts him and [[Troy (TV series)|Sheriff Troy]] to whom he claims he killed the man's father during [[The Target|a shootout]] in [[Filly]], escalating Troy's anger further until Booker diffuses the tension and orders his men to take their guest out and feed him to the hogs. However, when Troy attempts to grab the Ghoul, the bounty hunter retaliates and swiftly disarms the Govermint lackey along with [[Rex (TV series)|Sheriff Rex]], and both are gunned down by the Ghoul, to Booker's chagrin. The Ghoul is momentarily distracted from dealing with Booker when he notices the shack's selection of wanted posters, particularly the one of Lee Moldaver whom he recognizes, but instead by her name "Miss Williams" when he met her centuries ago, before the bombs.<ref name="FOTV0106">Events of {{FOTV|1|6}}</ref>

==Appearances==
The BBQ Shack appears {{In|FOTV}} episode "[[The Trap]]".

Soviet satellite.original_wikitext:
{{for|an overview of spacecraft|spacecraft}} {{Infobox location |games =FOTV |name =Soviet satellite |image =USSR Satellite TV.png |owners =[[Soviet Union]] (pre-War) |part of = }} The '''Soviet satellite''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.[[Michael Emerson]]: ''"That set in the Nevada desert with the downed Soviet satellite, it was, when I walked out there and saw that we were going to be performing in the shadow of this amazing prop, God..."''
[[Jonathan Nolan]]: ''"That's Howard Cummings, our production designer, is just, just incredible."''
([https://ageofthenerd.com/2024/04/exploring-the-fallout-universe-an-interview-with-jonathan-nolan-and-michael-emerson "Exploring the Fallout Universe: An Interview with Jonathan Nolan and Michael Emerson" from Age of the Nerd]) ==Background== Originally built by the [[Soviet Union]] before the [[Great War]], it was launched into orbit around the Earth, though any functions it may have carried out during this time are unknown. The satellite is painted red and was powered by two solar panels. The bottom of the satellite housed what seems to be a sophisticated camera and communications system, indicating that it was built largely for surveillance purposes. The camera was a large red spherical structure with the Russian abbreviation "СССР" emblazoned onto it. Sometime after the bombs fell in 2077, the satellite underwent orbital reentry and suffered significant damage when it landed in the flat plains close to the ruins of [[Los Angeles International Airport]] in [[New California]] but remained mostly intact, with some parts of its machinery still clearly visible.{{FOTV|1|2}} ==In the TV series== ===[[The Target]]=== After escaping from [[the Ghoul]] in [[Filly]], [[Lucy MacLean]] attempts to escort [[Siggi Wilzig]] across the plains near the old airport, however, he was slowed due to an injured leg shoddily "repaired" with a [[Jim's Limbs]] prosthetic that was causing him to deteriorate from blood loss. At some point before they reached the site of the crashed satellite, Wilzig ingested a [[Plan D]] cyanide pill to hasten his demise. Once this fact was revealed, he implores Lucy to use his [[surgical Ripper]] and remove his head containing the [[cold fusion]] artifact in order to carry it the rest of the way to [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] before passing away. After initial reluctance, Lucy performs the surgical removal and leaves the headless body propped up against the old satellite, where it is later found by the Ghoul who was following after [[CX404]] and her canine nose detecting Wilzig's scent. ===[[The Head]]=== Wilzig's corpse and the satellite are visited for a third time by [[Thaddeus]] and [[Maximus]] (disguised as [[Titus|Knight Titus]]) who discern that the artifact they were sent to find for the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] is embedded in the deceased's head, sending them after Lucy and the Ghoul. ==Appearances== The Soviet satellite appears {{in|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]]s "[[The Target]]" and "[[The Head]]." ==Behind the scenes== The appearance of the Soviet satellite in the ''Fallout'' TV series is the second occurrence of post-[[Divergence]] Soviet technology in the [[canon]] of the [[Fallout series|''Fallout'' series]], after the [[Assault rifle (Fallout)|AK-112 assault rifle]] in the ''[[Fallout]]'' video game. A special encounter in ''[[Fallout Tactics]]'' involved discovering the [[Mir]] space station but there is no in-universe evidence of its ownership past its name; after the whole of ''Fallout Tactics'' was declared non-canon and eventually transitioned into dubious canon, it no longer qualifies. ==Gallery== FOTV s1 ep2 LAX.png|Lucy and Wilzig approach the satellite FOTV Soviet satellite.png|The Ghoul and CX404 investigate Sovietsatelliteclose.png|Closeup ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} {{Navbox spacecraft}} {{Navbox vehicles}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Satellites]] [[Category:Soviet Union]] [[de:Sowjetischer Satellit]] [[ru:Разбившийся советский спутник]]

The '''Red Rocket''' '''gas station''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
One of many franchise locations across the [[United States of America|United States]] owned by the pre-[[Great War|War]] [[Red Rocket]] company, this particular gas station is located somewhere in the greater [[Los Angeles]] area. It features a [[Nuka-Cola]] cooler and [[Nuka-Cola vending machine|vending machine]], as well as a milk vending machine.

By the late 23rd century, parts of it have become overgrown but the structure itself remains largely intact.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Radio]]===
[[Thaddeus]] attempts to cross the wasteland carrying [[Siggi Wilzig]]'s head containing the [[cold fusion]] artifact. However, he is hampered both by his mangled foot after it was accidentally crushed by [[Maximus]]' [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]] during [[The Past|their scuffle]], and by the relentless pursuit by Wilzig's canine [[CX404]] trying to retrieve his head. When Thaddeus reaches the abandoned gas station, he does a brief examination of his injured foot, then notices the old Nuka-Cola cooler. He opts to lock the dog in there to prevent her from interfering, making an empty promise to come back later as he limps away.<ref name="FOTV0107">Events of {{FOTV|1|7}}</ref>

Sometime later, [[the Ghoul]], following the trail of the head, comes to the gas station and hears CX404's whimpering. After letting her out of the cooler, he begrudgingly adopts her as his own companion.<ref name="FOTV0107"/>

==Appearances==
The Red Rocket gas station appears only in the ''Fallout'' TV series episode "[[The Radio]]."

==Behind the scenes==
* Scenes set at the Red Rocket gas station were filmed at a real gas station in Nyack, New York,<ref group="Meta">[https://www.google.com/maps/place/Gulf+Gas+Station/@41.1094682,-73.929406,17z/data=!4m14!1m7!3m6!1s0x89c2c1faf964ec69:0xc322c59da11ce50f!2sGulf+Gas+Station!8m2!3d41.1094682!4d-73.9268311!16s%2Fg%2F11c1pr86yz!3m5!1s0x89c2c1faf964ec69:0xc322c59da11ce50f!8m2!3d41.1094682!4d-73.9268311!16s%2Fg%2F11c1pr86yz?entry=ttu Gulf Gas Station - Google Maps]</ref> which went on sale in 2020.<ref group="Meta">[https://www.reddit.com/r/mildlyinteresting/comments/hc8cag/this_gulf_station_in_upper_nyack_ny_was_most/ This Gulf station in Upper Nyack, N.Y. was most famous as a Levron. Propane is for sale, but the John Wick Mustang is not. - Reddit]</ref> The gas station has also served as a film set for the [[wikipedia:Keanu Reeves|Keanu Reeves]] film ''[[Wikipedia:John Wick (film)|John Wick]]''.<ref group="Meta">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rGGoNRUaVQI John Wick | Gas Station Scene | "How Much For The Car?" | Movie Clip (2014) - Youtube]</ref>
** According to production designer [[Howard Cummings]], the showrunners did not originally intend for a Red Rocket station to appear in the TV series until he made a request to create one. The owner of the Nyack gas station allowed the film crew to use it for a period of five days; the set was built in three days, shooting occurred in one day, and the last day was used to take down the set.<ref group="Meta">[https://archive.ph/FnGR8 Bringing Fallout’s gritty retrofuturism into the real world]</ref>
* The Ghoul encountering CX404 (whom he later nicknames "Dogmeat") at the Red Rocket gas station is a reference to ''[[Fallout 4]]'', in which the [[Sole Survivor]] meets that game's [[Dogmeat (Fallout 4)|Dogmeat]] at a [[Red Rocket truck stop]].

Hawthorne Medical Laboratories.original_wikitext:
{{Infobox faction |games =FOTV |image =FOTV Hawthorne Medical Laboratories.png |founded by = |leader =[[Lloyd Hawthorne]] (pre-War)
[[Cassandra Hawthorne]] (pre-War) |headquarters =[[Los Angeles]] campus |parent =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] (pre-War) |related =[[Vault 4]] }} '''Hawthorne Medical Laboratories''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Founded in the pre-[[Great War|War]] era, Hawthorne Medical Laboratories was a subsidiary of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]. Its main campus in [[Los Angeles]], [[State#California|California]] was connected to the structure of [[Vault 4]], which was designed as a research facility to be overseen by HML leaders [[Lloyd Hawthorne|Lloyd]] and [[Cassandra Hawthorne]]. The exterior entrance of Vault 4 was built not far from the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories campus, with the two locations in visible distance of each other. To aid in the [[radiation]] and genetics experiments of the Vault's head researchers, the surface-level building was altered such that a hallway just inside from the main entrance was turned into a booby-trapped chamber, luring people in by using a fake door labeled as the entrance to a medical storage wing, then dropping them down a chute into a decontamination room within Vault 4 where they would be processed as new test subjects. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Past]]=== Due to [[Maximus]]' health declining from a wound he sustained during the ambush by fiends [[Javin]] and [[Rink]], [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] helps him search for medical supplies. They eventually reach the grounds of Hawthorne Medical Laboratories, though do not notice the signage marking it as a Vault-Tec property. After Lucy fails to re-emerge from scouting ahead, Maximus enters himself and is caught in the booby trap that brings him and Lucy into Vault 4.Events of {{FOTV|1|6}} ===[[The Radio]]=== After being exiled from Vault 4 over Lucy's transgressing into Level 12 and Maximus' unwitting attack on the peaceful Vault dwellers trying to rescue her, she convinces him to make slight amends by returning the fusion core he took from their reactor to power his [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]]. The two briefly return to the medical campus to deposit the core through the trapdoor, where it's found by a Vault janitor who indirectly thanks them.Events of {{FOTV|1|7}} Before leaving, Maximus opens up to Lucy, revealing his true name and that he allowed the real [[Titus|Knight Titus]] to die; Lucy forgives him and admits to some of her own crimes (as she sees them) during her wasteland journey. She extends a heartfelt welcome to join her in [[Vault 33]] after they rescue [[Hank MacLean|her father]] from [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]], to which he agrees as they depart to find [[Cold fusion|the artifact]] taken by [[Thaddeus]]. ==Appearances== Hawthorne Medical Laboratories appears {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episodes]] "[[The Past]]" and "[[The Radio]]." ==Behind the scenes== * Pre-release images showing the name of Hawthorne Medical Laboratories were leaked to the public by u/PrinceDaCat on Reddit. * Scenes set at the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories campus were filmed at [[wikipedia:Bayley Seton Hospital|Bayley Seton Hospital]] in [[wikipedia:Staten Island|Staten Island, New York]]. ==Gallery== FOTV Hawthorne recreated_no_bottom.png|Hawthorne Medical Laboratories logo FOTV Hawthorne Logo.png|Full version of the van livery FOTV Hawthorne Medical Laboratories 2.png|Aerial view of the campus FOTV Hawthorne Medical Laboratories 3.png|[[Maximus]] explores the Hawthorne lobby FOTV Hawthorne Medical Labs Vault 4.png|Hawthorne Medical Laboratories; Vault 4 surface entrance visible in the distance Vault 4 entrance.jpg|Vault 4's surface entrance; the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories are visible to the left in the distance ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series mentioned-only organizations]] [[Category:Vault-Tec Corporation]] [[Category:Pre-War companies]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[de:Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]] [[ru:Медицинские лаборатории Хоторна]]
